governing: bolts (shear rupture of 2 x 3/4 in A325-N bolts through the column web, Ra 15.843 kip vs Rn/Omega 23.86 kip)
notes: ASD, Ra = 15.843 kip. Seat L4x4x1/2 A36, 6 in long, 4 in leg under the beam, 1/2 in setback (3/4 in with the 1/4 in underrun). Required bearing length is k = 0.747 in (J10.2 minimum; web local yielding and crippling need less), available 3.25 in. Utilisations: bolt shear 0.66; beam web crippling 0.65 at the 3.25 in available bearing (0.82 if bearing is taken as only k); seat outstanding-leg flexure 0.49 (Manual Part 10 model, critical section t + 3/8 in from the back of the angle, e = 0.25 in); web local yielding 0.37 (0.73 at lb = k); seat leg shear yield 0.37; bolt bearing 0.40 on the 0.34 in column web and 0.30 on the angle. Seat flexure is sensitive to the method: a 3/8 in angle fails under the Manual model (0.3735 in eccentricity, about 1.3), so 1/2 in is the lightest listed thickness that works; if the critical section were taken at the angle face instead of the fillet toe, the 1/2 in seat would be over capacity, so this design relies on the AISC Manual Part 10 convention. Fit: 6 in seat within the W10x49 web flat T = 7.5 in; beam flange 5.5 in within the 8.88 in between column flanges; bolt edge distances 1.25 in along the angle and 2 in on the vertical leg (min 1 in); bolt 2 in from the heel, clearing the 7/8 in fillet and leaving 1.5 in to the seat leg for the wrench. Bolt bearing on the column web assumes no beam bolted to the far side of the web through the same bolts. Two erection bolts through the beam's bottom flange into the seat and the top angle's bolts are detailed per standard practice and are not strength elements.
